figures.cap: regular hexagon ABCDEF divided into two triangles and a rectangle

parts.latex:
A regular hexagon of side length 5 cm is shown below.

\exfigure{717_q30_1}

The hexagon has been divided into two triangles $AEF$ and $BDC$, and a rectangle $ABDE$, as shown above.

Show that the area of the hexagon is approximately $65\text{ cm}^2$.

solutions.latex:
Each interior angle of a regular hexagon is $120^\circ$, so $\angle AFE=120^\circ$.

Using the cosine rule in $\triangle AEF$:
$$\begin{aligned} AE^2 &= 5^2+5^2-2\times 5\times 5\times\cos 120^\circ \\ &= 25+25-50\cos 120^\circ \\ &= 75 \end{aligned}$$
$$AE \approx 8.7 \text{ cm}$$
Area of $\triangle AEF$:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times 5\times 5\times\sin 120^\circ \\ &\approx 10.8 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$
Area of rectangle $ABDE$:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 8.7\times 5 \\ &= 43.5 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$
The hexagon is two triangles plus the rectangle.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area of hexagon} &= (2\times 10.8)+43.5 \\ &\approx 65 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the areas of the triangle and the rectangle, or equivalent merit
Finds $\angle AFE$ or sets up the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Both triangles share the angle $A$, so use the area formula with two sides and the included angle.
$$\text{Area}_{\triangle ABC} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 4 \times \sin A = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 12 \times \sin A$$
$$\text{Area}_{\triangle ADE} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 7 \times 10 \times \sin A = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 70 \times \sin A$$
The ratio is
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{1}{2} \times 12 \times \sin A : \dfrac{1}{2} \times 70 \times \sin A &= 12 : 70 \\ &= 6 : 35 \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is C.

solutions.latex:

$$A = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 17$$

figures.cap: quadrilateral ABCD with diagonal BD
solution sketch: quadrilateral with angles marked

solutions.latex:
Split the quadrilateral into triangles $ABD$ and $BCD$ using diagonal $BD$.

\exfigure{714_q29_s1}

In right-angled triangle $ABD$, by Pythagoras' theorem:
$$BD^2 = 6^2 + 9.5^2$$
$$BD = \sqrt{126.25}$$
In triangle $BCD$, by the cosine rule:
$$\cos \angle BCD = \dfrac{15.61^2 + 10^2 - \left(\sqrt{126.25}\right)^2}{2 \times 15.61 \times 10}$$
$$\angle BCD = 45.859^\circ = 45^\circ 51' \approx 46^\circ$$
The area is the sum of the two triangles.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9.5 \times 6 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 15.61 \times 10 \times \sin 45.859^\circ \\ &= 84.511\ldots \\ &\approx 84.5 \text{ km}^2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds $\angle BCD$ and sets up the area of both triangles, or equivalent merit
Finds $BD$ and sets up the cosine rule, or equivalent merit
